NASA1-VT6 là đội thi gồm 6 học sinh Trường THCS Vĩnh Trại, tỉnh Lạng Sơn. Đội trưởng là Nguyễn Võ Nhật Khánh, dưới sự hướng dẫn của cô giáo Hồ Minh Hằng.

Chúng em yêu thích khoa học, công nghệ, khám phá vũ trụ và lập trình. Đội mong muốn xây dựng trò chơi tương tác giúp học sinh tìm hiểu cuộc sống của các phi hành gia trên Mặt Trăng hoặc Sao Hỏa, sử dụng tài nguyên khoa học của NASA.

Khẩu hiệu: Đoàn kết – Sáng tạo – Chinh phục vũ trụ!
summary:
What does our team do?
NASA1-VT6 develops SELENE – Lunar Odyssey, an interactive lunar astronaut training game for young learners. Players explore the Moon, manage resources, and make decisions to keep their lunar base operational.
What problem does our project solve?
Our project addresses the challenge of helping students understand and practice essential astronaut skills through interactive experiences rather than traditional theoretical learning.
Why is this problem important?
Living and working on the Moon requires scientific knowledge, problem-solving skills, and good decision-making. Our game makes these challenges engaging and accessible while inspiring young people to explore space.
details:
SELENE – Lunar Odyssey v2.2

Team NASA1-VT6 | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Project Overview

SELENE – Lunar Odyssey is an interactive 2D educational game designed to help young students experience the challenges of managing a lunar outpost. Developed for Challenge #3, “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer,” the project transforms space science concepts into an engaging, decision-based learning experience.

Players become junior astronauts responsible for surviving a seven-day mission on the Moon. They must manage oxygen, food, health, and electrical power while repairing equipment, responding to simulated hazards, and conducting scientific exploration with NOVA, a robotic companion.

Our goal is to make space science more accessible by allowing students to learn through exploration, experimentation, and problem-solving.

How Does It Work?

At the beginning of each mission day, players select an energy management strategy. Their decisions influence power consumption, charging efficiency, and research rewards.

Players explore the lunar environment, collect tools, repair essential systems, and manage limited supplies. They must also monitor oxygen and food levels, recharge NOVA, and take shelter during dangerous events such as simulated radiation storms and micrometeorite hazards.

NOVA assists with collecting simulated lunar samples. Players deliver these samples to the research station, where they receive educational reports and scientific explanations.

The mission progresses through seven days. Successful completion requires balancing resources, maintaining essential systems, and making responsible decisions.

The game also includes optional quizzes, guidance, and a final assessment covering five areas: survival, resource management, base operations, scientific research, and knowledge.

NASA Science and Educational Value

SELENE incorporates educational references from NASA resources covering lunar conditions, environmental control and life-support systems, lunar regolith, radiation protection, and the Moon's South Pole.

The current version includes nine science cards with links to NASA reference materials. These resources help students understand the scientific reasoning behind mission challenges.

Importantly, SELENE is an educational simulation. Its resource values, sample reports, terrain, and hazard events are simplified or fictional. The game does not use live NASA APIs, real-time measurements, or actual lunar samples.

By distinguishing scientific references from simulation assumptions, we aim to encourage scientific curiosity and critical thinking.

Innovation and Creativity

SELENE combines several educational elements in one interactive experience:

  • A seven-day lunar survival mission with limited resources.
  • A robotic companion, NOVA, that follows the astronaut, collects samples, and requires battery management.
  • Resource trade-offs involving energy, oxygen, food, repairs, and scientific research.
  • Simulated environmental hazards that encourage risk assessment and shelter planning.
  • NASA-linked science explanations integrated into gameplay.
  • Quizzes, feedback, and a mission assessment that make player decisions visible.

Instead of simply presenting information about the Moon, SELENE gives students opportunities to apply scientific ideas through practical decisions.

Technology and Development Tools

SELENE was developed as a lightweight browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

The project uses a custom game engine and interface implemented in JavaScript, without requiring external runtime libraries or live APIs.

It can run offline in modern browsers such as Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge. Keyboard and touch controls make the game accessible across different devices.

Development and testing tools include Python for packaging, Node.js for automated tests, Git/GitHub for source-code management, and OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex for AI-assisted planning, programming, documentation, and testing.

The game itself does not require an AI service or internet connection to operate. Internet access is only needed when opening external NASA reference links.

Expected Impact and Benefits

SELENE is designed to help young learners develop an interest in space exploration, scientific reasoning, resource management, and problem-solving.

By managing a simulated lunar base, students can explore why life-support systems, energy availability, environmental protection, and limited supplies are important for space missions.

The project may also support classroom discussions and independent learning through interactive scenarios and science-based explanations.

Because SELENE is browser-based and supports offline play, it has the potential to reach students with limited internet access.

These are intended educational benefits. Formal classroom testing and measured learning outcomes have not yet been completed.

Design Considerations and Future Development

Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, educational value, player engagement, and technical feasibility.

We prioritized a simple interface, clear instructions, offline operation, limited resource systems, and transparent explanations of simulated data.

We also considered the importance of acknowledging NASA sources and distinguishing real scientific information from fictional game mechanics.

Future development may include classroom testing, teacher guidance, English-language localization, additional food-production scenarios, and activities involving traceable NASA datasets.

SELENE is currently a playable educational prototype. Our long-term vision is to develop it into a more comprehensive learning platform that inspires the next generation of space explorers.

Our message: Learn by exploring. Think like an astronaut. Make every decision count.
